clue.text: Star to take leading role in Titanic?

parts.note: to take the leading role in something is to head it
the Titanic was a famous ocean liner

explanation.surface: Asks which star will play the lead in the film Titanic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Titanic is the ship, not the film: to head the liner.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-billed performer, the main attraction on a programme, is its star.

clue.text: Attacks worker a lot

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farmhand
bags of something means plenty of it

explanation.surface: A labourer is accused of committing many assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: To handbag is British slang for attacking someone verbally and forcefully, coined for Margaret Thatcher's style in meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb meaning to lambast or savage someone, as a politician might do to opponents.

clue.text: Rage displayed by fisherman when line's become detached

indicators.note: a part that has become detached is no longer there, so this letter comes out of the word

parts.note: an angler is someone who fishes with rod and line
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A fisherman loses his temper when his line snaps off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fury or wrath, a strong feeling of displeasure.

clue.text: Declare capital's gone right down after hearing tax rises

indicators.note: this second piece is placed following the sounded piece
what is heard is a word spoken, so this piece is entered as it sounds rather than as written

parts.note: a levy is a tax or charge

indicators.note: the capital (first) letter has travelled all the way down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: to state is to declare

explanation.surface: A complaint that a city has declined after news of a tax increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital's gone right down' means the first letter sinks to the foot of this down entry; 'capital' tempts as a city, but it is a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to float upward, so it stands for climbing into the air.

clue.text: Less than 50%, indeed

definitions.meaning: literally short of a half share

explanation.definitionFit: First a literal fraction below one in two, then a British idiom of strong agreement meaning very much so.

clue.text: Wife's needed little time, cooking apple

parts.note: a wife is jokingly a rib, from Eve made from Adam's rib; the 's adds S
T is the abbreviation for time
something cooking is on, happening or under way

explanation.surface: A wife needs a moment to bake with an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking apple' looks like a phrase, but 'cooking' gives ON; the Ribston Pippin is an old English apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ribston Pippin is a traditional English variety of eating fruit from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Stuffiness apparent before middle of duet in composition

indicators.note: this first piece comes ahead of the next one

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, airless atmosphere in a room

indicators.note: the central letters of the word duet are taken

explanation.surface: A stuffy room is noticeable midway through a duet performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal piece of music, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: Girl looking embarrassed to be hugged by footballers

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside the arms of the other piece

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the English game's governing body
someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: A girl blushes as she is embraced by footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a female first name.

clue.text: Where body is buried, several feet beneath stones, mostly

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits under the first one
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: gravel is a mass of small stones
a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: Describes a burial site deep under a heap of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery or churchyard is a burial ground for the dead.

clue.text: Formerly safe head leaves Oxford college

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, departs from the word

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A former head of a college who was once safe is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER for a safe is old thieves' slang, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter College is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Semi-desert area, say, in western half of Nevada

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
the western part of a word in an across entry is its left-hand half

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Comments on a semi-arid region in the western part of Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the arid region occupying southern Israel.

clue.text: Wear a belt, specially adapted for service

indicators.note: something specially adapted is altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to wear a belt that has been altered for a special occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'service' is a dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a set of plates, dishes and cutlery for the table.

clue.text: Religious classes held in part by volunteers? Cleric takes this on himself

indicators.note: one piece is contained within the other

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
RE is religious education, a school subject
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A school RE lesson taught partly by volunteers, while a priest takes charge personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes this on himself' looks like taking on a duty; it means putting it on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn on the head by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Bar for swinger supplied gin and ecstasy tablets, it's said

indicators.note: the pieces are to be spoken out loud, and the answer is spelt as they are heard

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching animals; ecstasy tablets are Es

explanation.surface: Someone was given gin and ecstasy pills, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin here is a snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes on which acrobats swing.

clue.text: Make a great effort? Get lost!

definitions.meaning: to take special trouble to do something
literally to leave the path you are on, wander off course

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for taking pains to help, read second literally as straying off one's route.

clue.text: Give direction to London footballers, a half-depleted team

parts.note: Leyton Orient is a London football club

indicators.note: a word depleted by half keeps only its first half

explanation.surface: A London football club is told its side has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a football club in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to point or align something in a particular direction.

clue.text: Minor streets bordering rocket-testing area? Most unusual

indicators.note: the outer piece lies on both sides of the inner piece

parts.note: two streets, each abbreviated ST
a range is an area for firing and testing missiles

explanation.surface: Asks about side streets around a missile range.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of strange: the oddest or weirdest of all.

clue.text: Not getting started? Here's specially-treated petrol

definitions.meaning: free of a lead, a head start, read whimsically
fuel made without the additive tetraethyl lead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleaded fuel; also, playfully, being given no head start.

clue.text: Sparky teacher in a dire mess — job insecure

indicators.note: something insecure is unstable and shaky, so these letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively teacher in a terrible muddle whose job is under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparky' is not lively: it points to Muriel Spark, who wrote the novel The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie about an Edinburgh schoolmistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolmistress heroine of Muriel Spark's novel is a fictional educator created by that author.

clue.text: English king almost had power to amass portions' of land

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Arthur was the legendary king of Britain
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: King Arthur nearly had the power to gather pieces of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe in 'portions'' is an OCR slip; ignore it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners pile soil around the base of a plant, heaping up loose soil.

clue.text: After brief but polite rejection, rising group writes music

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: 'no ta' is a short, polite way of saying no thanks

indicators.note: in a down entry a word rising is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: After a curt refusal, an up-and-coming band composes songs.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set music down in written symbols.

clue.text: Samples couturier originally stitched into short cover

indicators.note: sewn in means placed within the other piece
short means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a swathe is a wrapping or cover

indicators.note: the original letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Fashion designer's fabric samples stitched into a short cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch is a set of fabric pieces bound together, so it stands for a bundle of samples.

clue.text: Order a brew in trendy pub

indicators.note: to order letters is to arrange them, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders a beer in a fashionable bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a fashionable drinking place, more stylish than a traditional pub.

clue.text: Foundation is supporting former undergraduates

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: BAs are holders of a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A foundation supports graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: groundwork or footing on which something rests.

clue.text: Mug's taken combat vehicle on a road

indicators.note: in an across entry, 'on' places this piece next to the next ones

parts.note: a tank is an armoured fighting vehicle

explanation.surface: Somebody's mug has been taken by a tank on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug's taken' reads as a fool being conned; Mug is the drinking vessel and ''s taken' joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer drinking vessel with a handle.

clue.text: Irish fellow appearing with Opera North

parts.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi

explanation.surface: An Irishman performing with the company Opera North.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera North is a Leeds-based opera company; here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidan is a male name of Irish origin, borne by an Irish saint.

clue.text: Team's opening bowlers stumped when in? End of story!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken
this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: two bowler hats
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A cricket team's opening bowlers are baffled when they are batting.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumped is a way of being out in cricket; on the scorecard it is shortened to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation closing a matter: nothing more to be said.

clue.text: Sound of mountain bird

indicators.note: what something sounds like is how it is pronounced, so the piece is heard, not seen

parts.note: Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete, and another in Turkey

explanation.surface: The cry of a mountain bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: Attends gathering of male journalists

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
eds is short for editors

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a meeting of male journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attends' means pays attention to, not goes to; 'gathering of' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to something is to take notice of it, to listen.

clue.text: What could be perfect in a lesson of French or history?

definitions.text: What could be perfect in a lesson of French or history?

parts.words: What could be perfect in a lesson of French or history?
parts.note: in grammar the perfect is a verb form describing completed action, taught in French lessons; history deals with bygone times

explanation.definitionFit: The perfect is one of the verb forms for events already over.
